blogs.title: Strict Adherence is Not an Invitation to Legislate: Textualism in Insurance Cancellations
blogs.description: An analysis of the Fifth Circuit's refusal to read a 'signature requirement' into a Louisiana statute. This post explores the tension between the judicial mandate for 'strict adherence' to statutory procedures and the textualist principle that courts should not add requirements that the legislature omitted, specifically regarding what it means to 'certify' a statement in a commercial context.

blogs.title: From Filing Cabinets to API Calls: Redefining 'Receipt' for the Digital Age
blogs.description: This post examines the court's interpretation of 'receipt' and 'possession' in the context of automated web services. By treating an e-mail/web-service call as a valid statutory notice, the court signals a pragmatic shift in how traditional legal terms of art are applied to modern, computer-driven business processes, moving away from the need for physical custody of documents.

blogs.title: The Certification Gamble: Federalism and the Reluctance to Ask State Courts
blogs.description: A look at the Fifth Circuit's decision to decline certification of a state law question to the Louisiana Supreme Court. This post discusses the strategic and jurisdictional implications of the 'compelling reason' standard for certification and the risks federal courts take when interpreting ambiguous state statutes without the state's highest court's guidance.
